passages.text: Beschorneria yuccoides is a species of succulent plant belonging to the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Agavoideae.

Etymology
The epithet yuccoides is a compound of the botanical name of the genus Yucca and the Greek suffix -ό-εἶδος (o-eidos) oides meaning "likeness".

Subspecies
 Beschorneria yuccoides subsp. yuccoides
 Beschorneria yuccoides subsp. dekosteriana (K.Koch) Govaerts

Beschorneria yuccoides is a stemless plant with 20 to 35 linear, lanceolate, leathery leaves that are widened at their base. They are gray-green to green, about {{convert|40|-|60|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3.3|-|3.5|cm|abbr=on}} wide. The leaf margins are finely denticulate. The inflorescence reaches a height of {{convert|100|-|180|cm|abbr=on}}, with a maximum of {{convert|320 |cm|in|abbr=on}}. The stem and the bract are red. The flowers are 40 to 50 mm long. The fruits are elongated to almost spherical, {{convert|30|-|40|mm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|15|-|25|mm|abbr=on}} wide.

Distribution
Beschorneria yuccoides is present in Mexico, in the states of Hidalgo, Puebla and Veracruz, at an elevation of {{convert|2700|-|3000|m|abbr=on}} above sea level.

Cultivation
This plant is not tolerant of severe freezes, and is best suited to warm, sheltered south- or west-facing places in full sun, where temperatures do not fall below {{convert|-5|C|F}}. Alternatively, it can be grown under glass.
It grows outdoors at Earlscliffe, Howth, County Dublin, Ireland, at a latitude of 53.3º N, where it benefits from the unusually favourable microclimate.
In cultivation in the UK it has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.
